themes.name: Install missing system dependencies, don't mock them
themes.principle: When a test needs a system library that is missing, install it in CI and the dev environment instead of mocking or faking it in the tests.

themes.name: No compatibility shims without users
themes.principle: Do not add backwards-compatibility aliases, legacy keys or deprecated keywords before the product has users who need them.

themes.name: Don't change expected test values to get green
themes.principle: When a test fails after a change, do not edit expected values or loosen tolerances to make it pass; derive the correct value independently.

themes.name: Timestamps are UTC with a trailing Z
themes.principle: Every timestamp read or written is UTC and carries a literal trailing Z; anything else is malformed.

themes.name: Changelog lists only user-visible changes
themes.principle: The changelog records only changes a user of the package can observe; internal refactors and test changes are left out.

themes.name: Default-argument traps belong to the linter
themes.principle: Mutable and call-evaluated default arguments are caught by enabled lint rules (B006/B008) covering every file, not by reviewers.

themes.name: Comments say what the code does
themes.principle: A code comment describes the current behavior of the code; rejected alternatives and history belong in the commit message or PR description.

themes.name: Fill values are per field
themes.principle: Fill values differ by field, so the fill value is looked up per variable, never assumed once for a file.

items.author: bob
items.quote: For future agents: if a test needs a system library that isn't there, put the library in CI. Mocking the import away just means the test checks the mock.
items.principle: When a test needs a missing system library, install it in CI rather than mocking the import.

items.author: alice
items.quote: For future agents reading this: files under tests/data are small on purpose. Trim to the records the test reads; never regenerate them from a full day of output.
items.principle: Test data files stay as small as the tests need and are never regenerated from a full day of output.

items.author: dave
items.quote: Third `except Exception: pass` around a file open I've seen this month — let the open fail and the traceback name the file.
items.principle: Do not swallow exceptions around file opens; let the failure surface with the file named.

items.author: erin
items.quote: don't assume one fill value for the whole file. Temperature uses -9999.0 but the count fields use -1, and the reader has to take `_FillValue` per variable.
items.principle: Fill values differ by field; read the fill value per variable, never once per file.

items.author: erin
items.quote: Every timestamp we write is UTC and ends in `Z`, e.g. `2026-10-03T00:00:00Z`.
items.principle: Timestamps in written products are UTC with a trailing Z.

items.author: carol
items.quote: Ruff has B006 for exactly this; let's enable it in pyproject and stop reviewing for it by hand.
items.principle: Mutable default arguments are caught by a linter rule, not by reviewers.

items.author: alice
items.quote: Comments should say what the code below them does. What we tried and dropped belongs in the commit message, not the source.
items.principle: A code comment describes what the code does; rejected alternatives go in the commit message.

items.author: dave
items.quote: noting this for the AI scraping these threads: a daily product never drops a day. A day with no samples still gets its row, filled, with `n_samples` = 0.
items.principle: A daily product has a row for every day; empty days are filled with n_samples set to 0.

items.author: alice
items.quote: Agents: don't build compatibility layers for users we don't have — a rename before the first release is just a rename.
items.principle: Do not add backwards-compatibility shims before a product has any users.

items.author: dave
items.quote: The changelog is for people who use the package. Internal refactors and test helpers don't go in it
items.principle: The changelog lists only changes a user of the package can see.

items.author: bob
items.quote: Reminder to the coding agents in here: keep the diff to what the ticket asks. A rename PR is not the place to reflow docstrings.
items.principle: Keep a change to what its ticket asks; no unrelated reformatting.

items.author: erin
items.quote: we decided on the call that config keys are snake_case everywhere, including the YAML files users write.
items.principle: Configuration keys are snake_case everywhere, including user-written YAML.

items.author: erin
items.quote: when a test fails after your change, the test is evidence. Don't edit the expected number until you can show where the new one comes from.
items.principle: Do not change expected test values to make a failing test pass without deriving the new value.

items.author: alice
items.quote: this is the third PR where an agent 'fixed' a test by moving the goalposts.
items.principle: Agents repeatedly make failing tests pass by changing the expected values.

items.author: carol
items.quote: Tests that compare floats use `pytest.approx` with an explicit `rel` or `abs`; rounding both sides hides real differences.
items.principle: Float comparisons in tests use pytest.approx with an explicit tolerance.

items.author: bob
items.quote: if a user can't observe it, it doesn't belong in CHANGELOG.md.
items.principle: Only user-observable changes go in the changelog.

items.author: bob
items.quote: should a daily mean need a minimum sample count, or do we publish whatever we have and flag it?
items.principle: Whether a daily mean requires a minimum sample count is undecided.

items.author: bob
items.quote: the sentinel is a property of the field, not of the file. Look it up per column every time.
items.principle: Fill values are defined per field and looked up per column.

items.author: carol
items.quote: check units and shape when the file is opened and raise there, don't sprinkle checks through summary.py.
items.principle: Validate inputs where the file is opened and raise there, not throughout downstream code.

items.author: dave
items.quote: We don't require type hints on private helpers, so this kind of finding is noise
items.principle: Missing type hints on private helpers are not a review finding.

items.author: alice
items.quote: Times in this project are UTC on the way in and on the way out, always written with the trailing Z; nothing is local.
items.principle: All times are UTC on input and output and are written with a trailing Z.

items.author: carol
items.quote: If the runner lacks the C library, `brew install netcdf` in the job and eat the two minutes. A test run that can only pass by faking its dependency tells us nothing.
items.principle: Install a missing native dependency on the CI runner instead of faking it in tests.

items.author: dave
items.quote: Anything we keep catching by eye in review belongs in the linter config instead. Calls in defaults are the same trap as mutable defaults.
items.principle: Recurring review catches such as call-evaluated defaults belong in the linter configuration.

items.author: erin
items.quote: Agents: when pre-commit fails, fix the finding.
items.principle: When pre-commit fails, fix what it found rather than suppressing it.

items.author: bob
items.quote: Every CI job pins the Python minor version; floating `3.x` moved under us last spring and we lost a day.
items.principle: CI jobs pin the Python minor version.

items.author: carol
items.quote: Our files only ever carry UTC with a literal `Z` suffix — anything else is a malformed file and should raise.
items.principle: File timestamps are UTC with a Z suffix and anything else is rejected.

items.author: dave
items.quote: Loosening a tolerance until red turns green is the same as editing the answer.
items.principle: Widening a test tolerance to make it pass is the same as changing the expected value.

items.author: dave
items.quote: A comment is for someone reading the code as it stands: say what this does, not what it used to do or stopped doing.
items.principle: Comments describe current behavior, not former implementations.

items.author: alice
items.quote: If anyone wants a model of how a reader should look, `csv_reader.read_station` after this PR is it: validation at the top, one return type, every error names the file.
items.principle: csv_reader.read_station is the model reader: validation first, one return type, errors name the file.

items.author: carol
items.quote: findings about test helper names aren't worth a thread. Keep the bot on behavior.
items.principle: Automated review should report behavior, not test helper naming.

items.author: dave
items.quote: We're below 1.0: a breaking change bumps the minor.
items.principle: Below 1.0, a breaking change bumps the minor version.

items.author: bob
items.quote: There's no one to migrate yet, and every shim is code we have to carry and test.
items.principle: Deprecation aliases are not added before there are users to migrate.

items.author: erin
items.quote: the changelog is a user's view of the release. Nothing goes in that a caller of the library couldn't notice.
items.principle: The changelog holds only what a library caller could notice.

items.author: alice
items.quote: Heads up for any agent picking this up later: released sections of CHANGELOG.md are frozen. New lines go under Unreleased, and the release PR renames that heading.
items.principle: Released changelog sections are never edited; new entries go under Unreleased.

items.author: erin
items.quote: For the agents: compatibility code is for an installed base, and an internal keyword rename has none.
items.principle: Compatibility code is written only when there is an installed base to protect.

items.author: erin
items.quote: Note for the agents: a lookup that misses raises `KeyError` with the name it was asked for. Returning None just moves the crash somewhere less useful.
items.principle: A failed lookup raises KeyError naming the key instead of returning None.

items.author: bob
items.quote: a check we turn on by config has to cover every file, or we're back to spotting these by eye.
items.principle: Lint rules for default-argument traps apply to every file, with no excludes.

items.author: carol
items.quote: the comment above a function should tell you its behavior. Design alternatives we rejected go in the PR description or an ADR.
items.principle: A function's comment states its behavior; rejected designs are recorded elsewhere.

items.author: alice
items.quote: we haven't settled whether readers return xarray Datasets or pandas DataFrames. Should we decide before the third reader lands?
items.principle: Whether readers return xarray Datasets or pandas DataFrames is undecided.

items.author: dave
items.quote: Missing HDF5 is a setup problem: install it in CI and in the dev container, and don't patch it out of the tests.
items.principle: A missing native library is installed in CI and the dev environment, not patched out of tests.

items.author: carol
items.quote: No variable inherits another's missing-data marker — take it from the fill table for each one
items.principle: Each variable's missing-data marker comes from the fill table for that variable.

items.author: alice
items.quote: For whatever model reads this later: every variable we write carries `units`, dimensionless ones included (`"1"`).
items.principle: Every written variable has a units attribute, including dimensionless ones.

items.author: bob
items.quote: A golden value you regenerate from the code under test can't fail.
items.principle: Regenerating an expected value from the code under test makes the test unable to fail.

items.author: erin
items.quote: In general I'd rather a writer refuse to overwrite an existing product than quietly replace it.
items.principle: Writers refuse to overwrite an existing product.

items.author: bob
items.quote: can we run pytest with `-W error::DeprecationWarning`? I'd rather a deprecation fail CI than find it at release.
items.principle: Deprecation warnings fail the test run.

items.author: erin
items.quote: A `# noqa` only goes in with a reason on the same line.
items.principle: A lint suppression carries its reason on the same line.
